item.title: [Itrfoundation] A Few Votes, Long-Term Consequences: Results from Iowa’s September 2026 Special Elections
item.description:
Iowa voters approved 22 of 26 public measures on September 8, including 14 of 18 Physical Plant and Equipment Levy (PPEL) questions, all four school Revenue Purpose Statements (RPS), and all three city and county tax measures. The results included several notable decisions. Dubuque voters approved doubling the district’s PPEL after rejecting a $70 million bond last year. Clarinda voters rejected another school tax proposal even after the district substantially reduced its request. Webster City voters approved two PPEL questions that together provide maximum taxing authority for roughly 13 years. And in Van Meter, a PPEL renewal passed by just two votes.

A new Iowans for Tax Relief Foundation (ITRF) poll of likely general election voters in Iowa reveals consistent support for fending off tax hikes, and a political environment that is pointing toward close races up and down the ballot. The survey, conducted from June 16-19, 2026 , found that support for an amendment to Iowa’s constitution requiring a two-thirds supermajority of the state legislature to approve income tax increases has grown to 73.8%, up from 70.5 % last September. This strong backing extends across political lines; 72% of independent voters and 60% of democrat voters favor this protection.

The post New Poll: Iowa Voters Support Supermajority Requirement to Raise Income Taxes appeared first on ITR Foundation.
